person.name: Lior Milliger
person.headline: Platform Engineer · DevOps & Cloud Infrastructure · AI Systems Architect
person.summary: Platform Engineer and AI Systems Architect with 3+ years building production infrastructure end-to-end, from cloud-native Kubernetes platforms to edge and air-gapped environments. AWS SAA and CKA certified. Specializes in microservices migrations, GitOps automation and AI-driven pipelines.
about: Experienced DevOps and Infrastructure Engineer, taking end-to-end ownership of production environments, from bare-metal and edge devices to highly available Kubernetes clusters.

Specialized in Kubernetes architecture, Helm chart design, and CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Bitbucket Pipelines) with GitOps automation (FluxCD, ArgoCD). Hands-on with Ansible for zero-touch provisioning and k3s for air-gapped edge deployments, including full monolith-to-Kubernetes migrations for production environments.

Designing multi-region AWS platforms (CloudFormation, SAM) with VPN-first architectures (WireGuard) linking edge deployments to cloud-hosted services. Layered IaC with Terraform, Terragrunt, and CloudFormation for modular, reusable infrastructure.

Building agentic AI systems and organizational knowledge infrastructure, including an Organizational Brain reasoning layer, an AI-awareness layer, and multi-session Claude architectures. Working with LangChain, embedding models, and Qdrant to power retrieval and memory for these pipelines.

What drives him is ownership: seeing a system through from design to production, and being the person a team can rely on when something breaks. Picks up new tools and domains fast, thrives on ambiguity, and believes the best infrastructure gets built by teams that trust each other.

timeline.title: The Overture
timeline.text: Music career from the Jerusalem Academy of Music to the jazz clubs of New York City. Designed and implemented music-education networks for entire municipalities, founded and conducted a 20-piece big band. Recorded an album in NYC titled "Your Comfort Zone Will Kill You".

timeline.title: The Transition
timeline.text: Self-study bootcamps in Python and DevOps, then Develeap's 16-week hands-on DevOps bootcamp (Git, Jenkins, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Prometheus, Grafana, EFK). Earned AWS Cloud Practitioner, AWS Solutions Architect Associate and CKA.

timeline.title: First Movement: JFrog
timeline.text: DevOps Support Engineer for Infrastructure at JFrog, supporting enterprise customers' DevOps pipelines: logs, Java code, networking, performance and storage. A FinOps project using Terraform and Lambda to automate cost-saving across AWS Organizations eliminated 80% of cloud waste and cut monthly spend by 30%.

timeline.title: Second Movement: Platform & AI Engineering
timeline.text: At Polus Tech: owns the full migration of an edge intelligence platform to a 13-microservice K3s cluster, architects AI-Ops ingestion pipelines with RAG (n8n, S3 triggers, Qdrant), and engineers per-unit provisioning automation with Ansible. In a parallel role, building a full-stack web platform from scratch, owning frontend, backend, Kubernetes infrastructure and authentication end-to-end.

projects.name: Quorum
projects.summary: A collaborative GenAI workspace where teams work with Claude together in shared sessions: a Main channel where Claude's streamed answers are visible to everyone, a Slack-style team chat Claude reads for context, and a private one-on-one channel with Claude per person. Role-based access via AWS Cognito, shared connectors to MCP servers and Confluence, and living documents that Claude edits in real time with versioned red/green diffs and undo. Built end to end: architecture, backend, frontend, AWS IaC and test suites. Source is private.

projects.name: This website
projects.summary: This portfolio site, including its AI agent. Flask app with PostgreSQL, running in production with Docker Compose on AWS EC2 (Nginx, Certbot) to keep costs low, deployed by a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner. It is also built for Kubernetes: CI scans images with Gitleaks and Trivy, pushes to ECR and updates the mywebsite-k8s repo for ArgoCD GitOps on an EKS cluster provisioned with Terraform. Three repos: mywebsite-app, mywebsite-k8s, mywebsite-iac.

site_architecture.title: Production on EC2, ready for EKS
site_architecture.summary: To keep costs low, the site runs in production with Docker Compose on a single AWS EC2 instance: Nginx as the TLS reverse proxy, Certbot for Let's Encrypt certificates, the Flask app on gunicorn and PostgreSQL. A self-hosted GitHub Actions runner on the instance deploys every push to main. The same app is built to run on Kubernetes too: GitHub Actions builds the image, scans it with Gitleaks and Trivy, pushes it to AWS ECR and bumps the tag in the mywebsite-k8s repo, so ArgoCD can deploy it to an EKS cluster provisioned with Terraform (mywebsite-iac). The AI agent calls the Claude API with this profile as its only knowledge source; its API key comes from AWS Secrets Manager through the instance role, with a daily budget and per-visitor limits.
